verdict: Meta's revenue rose 16% to $42.3B as ad prices climbed 10% — and with costs growing only 9%, it kept $16.6B as profit, about 39 cents of every dollar, even as Reality Labs lost another $4.2B.

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: after $13.7B of capex incl. finance leases

kpis.label: Family DAP
kpis.note: people using Meta's apps daily, +6% YoY

segments.name: Advertising
segments.note: Ads across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger: impressions rose 5% and the average price per ad rose 10%.

segments.name: Family of Apps other revenue
segments.note: WhatsApp business messaging, Meta Verified subscriptions and other app income; up 34% YoY.

segments.name: Reality Labs
segments.note: Quest headsets and AI glasses; revenue fell 6% and the unit lost $4.2B this quarter.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: AI research, engineers and Reality Labs development; up 22% YoY.

opex.name: Marketing & sales
opex.note: Selling ads and marketing Meta's apps and devices.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Back-office and legal costs — well down from $3.5B a year ago.

follow100Note: Advertising is $97.82 of every $100 Meta takes in. The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
otherDetail: Meta reports one combined line, interest and other income (expense), net; this quarter it was an $827M net gain.

takeaways.title: Higher ad prices did the work
takeaways.text: Ad impressions rose 5% and the average price per ad rose 10%, powered by AI ad tools — advertising brought in $41.4B of the $42.3B total.

takeaways.title: Margins widened again
takeaways.text: Operating margin reached 41%, up from 38% a year ago, because revenue grew 16% while total costs grew only 9%.

takeaways.title: Reality Labs still burns cash
takeaways.text: The headsets-and-glasses unit lost $4,210M in one quarter on just $412M of revenue — the price Meta pays to build its next platform while the ad business funds it.
